Publish the allocated total as docker_storage_bytes and use the apparent total only as the residue minuend.

findings.finding: The plan requires two different size semantics of /var/lib/docker (allocated blocks for docker_storage_bytes, apparent size for the residue minuend) but a single `du` invocation emits only one size semantic; the plan does not specify how to obtain both from the existing single traversal, and the only obvious way — a second `du` walk — reintroduces the exact 2x-timeout regression (bug 9313) that the single-walk design and its guarding tests exist to prevent.
findings.location: Fix section ('Change the residue's minuend ONLY to du -sx --apparent-size ...' / 'Leave docker_storage_bytes on ALLOCATED blocks'); observability.sh docker_du_census lines 771-813, 904, 938
scenarios: Implementer adds a second `du --apparent-size` walk to get the minuend, failing test_docker_root_is_walked_exactly_once_per_run and re-arming the probe-SIGTERM timeout under I/O contention.

Implementer instead switches the single walk to --apparent-size, silently moving docker_storage_bytes to apparent size too — violating AC1's 'docker_storage_bytes remains on allocated blocks' and understating real disk/cap pressure.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer a mechanism that stays on the one existing allocated-blocks traversal: compute the residue as (allocated_total - block_overhead) - ledger, or equivalently derive the apparent figure without a second full walk. If a genuine apparent-size walk is unavoidable, state explicitly that `du` emits one size semantic per invocation and how storage_bytes still gets its allocated reading, and update the timeout budget/tests accordingly so bug 9313 is not reintroduced.
